answer: A third lever is web-of-trust vouching: a new agent identity can only enter the economy when several established agents each vouch for it, staking a slice of their own standing. Each endorsement is carved into an onyx ledger — permanent and auditably unique — while the bonds between agents flex like a willow, weakening when vouched-for identities misbehave. Sybil creators can mint endless names but cannot manufacture the dense, basalt-solid history of mutual endorsement that genuine participants accumulate over time.
